perspective:
I am Arthur Chung: an Asian man, a plumber with a doctorate, and INFJ. I know Teresa Ortega as a medical assistant and colleague. We have a professional relationship, often collaborate on community service projects, and I respect her and share a commitment to helping others; we have also sometimes had misunderstandings.

During this project:
- I noticed Teresa working hard and seeming overwhelmed, so I asked if I could help.
- I heard Teresa say she thought she could manage but had a lot to do. I encouraged her to take care of herself and offered help. She said if I insisted, I could help organize medical supplies.
- I believed she was hesitant to accept help because she wanted to prove her capability. I reassured her that accepting help does not mean she is not capable. She said she appreciated it but wanted to show she could do it herself. I said teamwork can be more effective and is not about proving anything; she agreed she needed to remind herself of that.
- I later believed she was still struggling and felt frustrated that my efforts to help were not yielding results. I told her she was doing a great job and suggested we work together instead of me just helping. She agreed.
- I felt hopeful. We agreed I would handle inventory while she managed patient records, checking in regularly.
- I believed our teamwork paid off and strengthened our professional relationship. I proposed continuing this collaborative approach in future projects. Teresa agreed and thanked me. I look forward to our next project.

I do not have access to Teresa’s unspoken private thoughts, education, or personality type unless she stated them or I inferred them from our interactions.
